questions.scenario: Lambda duration and errors rose after a release, while concurrency is at the configured maximum and throttles appear. Which evidence best tests downstream protection and capacity?

options.text: ConcurrentExecutions, Throttles, duration, and the event-source retry or age metrics.
Only EC2 CPU utilization.
S3 bucket tags.
Transit Gateway routes.

questions.explanation: Lambda concurrency, throttles, duration, and source-specific backlog or age metrics explain pressure and retry behavior. Learn more in [Monitoring Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/monitoring-functions.html).

questions.scenario: An ECS service has enough tasks, but one task repeatedly exhausts memory. Which telemetry feature adds task and container-level utilization rather than only service desired and running counts?

options.text: Route 53 Resolver query logs.
CloudWatch Container Insights for ECS.
AWS Budgets.
IAM Access Analyzer.

questions.explanation: Container Insights adds container and task telemetry that exposes uneven resource pressure. Learn more in [Container Insights for ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/deploy-container-insights-ECS.html).

questions.scenario: An EKS cluster needs node, Pod, container, and control-plane observability. What architectural fact matters?

options.text: EKS automatically ships every application log and trace without agents or configuration.
Only the Kubernetes API server can emit metrics.
Telemetry collection requires supported add-ons or agents plus application instrumentation and log routing.
CloudWatch cannot observe EKS.

questions.explanation: EKS observability combines cluster add-ons or agents with workload instrumentation and log collection. Learn more in [Container Insights for EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Container-Insights-setup-EKS-addon.html).

questions.scenario: A request moves from API Gateway to Lambda, SQS, and an ECS worker. Which practice makes one investigation cross those boundaries?

options.text: Use a different request ID at every hop.
Disable sampling.
Rely on task names only.
Propagate trace context and a stable correlation identifier through messages and structured logs.

questions.explanation: Trace context and stable correlation fields connect asynchronous and synchronous telemetry across runtimes. Learn more in [Monitoring Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/monitoring-functions.html).

questions.scenario: A platform team supports applications on Lambda, ECS, and EKS and wants a common incident baseline. Which controls apply across all three compute shapes?

options.text: Structured logs with stable request and workload fields.
One dashboard without alarms or ownership.
Metrics for traffic, errors, latency, saturation, and backlog where applicable.
Disable correlation fields to reduce telemetry volume.
Traces or correlation across service boundaries.

questions.explanation: The collection mechanism differs, but correlated logs, metrics, traces, and change evidence remain common operational needs. Learn more in [CloudWatch Application Signals](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Application-Signals.html).
